payload.origin: Router noticed an in_progress P0 with updated_at=null, provisionally read it as a stalled row, tried to corroborate before filing, and found the opposite — the row is actively worked. The FIELD is the defect, not the row.
payload.envelope_note: Enveloped with from/to/type so this file drains instead of pinning the inbox floor.

finding.title: task_board rows carry updated_at=null on 438 of 472 rows (~93%) — every age-based staleness or hygiene predicate on this board is reading null for almost the entire board
finding.owner_suggestion: po triage — likely pm (row-mutation contract) plus whoever owns the backlog-hygiene / BOUNDED-1 predicates. Router did NOT mint a row and did NOT backfill any timestamps.

measurement_verbatim.aggregate: 438 of 472 rows null. Only the ready lane populates it consistently (19/19).

finding.how_it_was_found_and_the_false_read_it_c: SPIKE-BCTC-EXTRACTION-DORMANT-MASS-ENRICHFAIL-FLOOD sits in in_progress, P0, created 2026-07-16T21:00:34Z, updated_at=null, updated_by=null. On the field alone that is a five-day-old P0 nobody has touched, occupying a WIP slot — the exact 'structurally stalled' signature. Corroboration refuted it: git log shows SEVEN commits against that row, including AC-2 findings (60bdca243), a PO escalation to P0 with an AC-3 circuit-breaker fast-track (91e973eab), a refine-fold transform (f7ac37bc0) and a cold-evict fold (d480f1031). The row is one of the more actively worked items on the board. Router was one step from filing a false stall escalation on it.
finding.why_this_is_more_than_cosmetic: The field reads as authoritative and is wrong in BOTH directions. False-positive: an active row looks abandoned (as above). False-negative, and this is the expensive one: a genuinely abandoned row is indistinguishable from an active one, because null is the norm rather than the exception. This is the plausible mechanism behind a documented six-week miss — FIX-AUDITOR-COMMIT-NONEXPLICIT-PATHSPEC was filed 2026-06-08 with owner:null/next_agent:null and idled six weeks while its defect fired twice more. An age-based sweep would have surfaced it; on this board such a sweep has ~7% coverage.
finding.relationship_to_known_backlog_problem: The 4-loop wiring audit already recorded that loops 2 and 4 stall in a 404-row backlog. That backlog is 399/407 null on updated_at. Any 'oldest untouched row' or 'age > N days' triage over it is effectively sorting on a constant. Worth checking whether the BOUNDED-1 predicates read updated_at, because if they do, their staleness gating has never actually discriminated.
finding.scope_boundary_router_did_not_verify: Router did NOT determine WHY the field is null — whether writers omit it, whether orch-apply strips it, or whether only certain mutation paths set it. Note that ready is 19/19 populated, so SOME path does write it correctly; that asymmetry is the lead worth pulling. Router also did not check whether created_at is similarly affected (it appeared populated on every row inspected, but that was not measured board-wide).

payload.do_not_over_correct: Do NOT mass-backfill updated_at from git history or from file mtime to make the field look populated. A fabricated timestamp is worse than a null one — null at least reads as 'unknown', whereas a synthesised value would make the staleness sweeps confidently wrong and would falsify the audit trail. Fix the write path first; decide separately and explicitly whether historical rows get a documented backfill or stay null.
payload.router_did_not: mint a board row, modify any task row, backfill any timestamp, or change any predicate.
